hints: Notice the liquid depth $h$ is stated to be the same in P and Q, while $\rho_P = 2\rho_Q$.
Recall hydrostatic pressure on the base depends only on depth and density through $p = h\rho g$, not on whether vessel P tapers outwards and Q tapers inwards.
Form the ratio $p_P / p_Q$ and cancel the common $h$ and $g$ to leave only the density ratio.
walkthrough: Identify the useful data: same vertical depth $h$ for both vessels, $\rho_P = 2\rho_Q$, and the 45-degree tapering which changes volume and weight but not the pressure rule.
State the governing physics: pressure due to a liquid column on its base is $p = h\rho g$.
Write each pressure: $p_P = h\rho_P g$ and $p_Q = h\rho_Q g$.
Divide to get the required ratio: $p_P / p_Q = (h\rho_P g)/(h\rho_Q g) = \rho_P / \rho_Q$.
Substitute $\rho_P = 2\rho_Q$: $p_P / p_Q = 2\rho_Q / \rho_Q = 2/1$. This is option A.

A.explanation: Pressure is $p = h\rho g$ with the same $h$, so the ratio equals the density ratio $2$ to $1$.

B.explanation: The $45^{\circ}$ sides do not introduce a factor of $\sqrt{2}$ because hydrostatic pressure depends only on vertical depth, not wall angle.

C.explanation: The inverse with $\sqrt{2}$ is incorrect because pressure increases with density and P has the larger density.

D.explanation: This inverts the density relationship; P contains the liquid twice as dense, so its base pressure is larger, not smaller.
